rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the first experiment must establish a strong multimodal baseline and reduce uncertainty about the most impactful design choices. config_008 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, transformer, weighted) tests the core hypothesis that combining RNA and image features with multiprofile transformer aggregation yields strong accuracy. It uses pca_n2000 (moderate-cost, 2000-dim linear representation) and resnet50 (solid but cheaper than ViT-L) to keep cost manageable while the transformer aggregation is the key expressive component being validated. If this performs well, it justifies investing in more expensive encoders (scgpt, ViT-L) in later experiments; if it underperforms, it signals that simpler aggregation or different encoders may suffice. Expected relative cost: moderate-to-high — transformer aggregation and multiprofile processing add overhead, but avoiding ViT-L and scgpt keeps it well below the most expensive configurations (e.g., config_041/035).

With only one completed experiment (config_008: multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, transformer, weighted → 0.573 acc, 6.61 GPU-hrs), the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality is actually contributing to performance or whether the RNA signal alone suffices. config_029 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, transformer) isolates this by removing the image encoder while keeping the same RNA encoder and transformer aggregation, making it a clean ablation. If RNA-only approaches or exceeds 0.573, the search can pivot toward cheaper unimodal or simpler multimodal configs; if it falls well short, multimodal fusion is confirmed as essential and I can focus remaining budget on optimizing image encoder and fusion strategy. Expected relative cost: roughly 3–4 GPU hours (no image encoder, but retains transformer aggregation and multiprofile processing), about half of config_008, preserving budget for subsequent experiments.

Evidence: config_008 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, transformer, weighted) is our best at 0.5729 acc but costs 6.61 GPU hrs, largely due to transformer aggregation. The RNA-only baseline (0.5191) confirms multimodal adds ~5% value. Question: Is the expensive transformer aggregation actually necessary, or does simple average pooling (avgpool) capture most of the multiprofile information at a fraction of the cost? This experiment (config_007) is a clean single-variable ablation of config_008 (transformer→avgpool, everything else identical), directly testing whether the ~4+ GPU hr premium of the transformer is justified. If avgpool matches or nearly matches 0.5729, we unlock much cheaper multimodal configs for the remaining 7 experiments, preserving budget for exploring image encoders and RNA encoders. If it falls short, we confirm transformer aggregation is critical and can confidently invest remaining budget in transformer-based variants. Expected cost: ~2–3 GPU hrs (roughly 40–50% of config_008), making it a high-information, low-cost experiment that reduces uncertainty about the most expensive architectural component before committing further budget.

Evidence: config_007 (avgpool + weighted fusion, pca_n2000, resnet50) achieved the best accuracy (0.639), and avgpool clearly outperforms transformer aggregation (0.639 vs 0.573 in config_008). The fusion method (weighted vs concat) is an untested design axis within the best-known architecture. This experiment tests whether concat fusion can match or exceed weighted fusion while keeping all other hyperparameters at their proven-best values (multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool). It is the most targeted, low-uncertainty next step: a single-variable change from the current best. If concat improves accuracy, it opens a new direction; if not, we confirm weighted fusion is optimal and can pivot to testing stronger image encoders (ViT-L) or learned RNA encoders. Expected cost: similar to config_007 (~10-11 GPU hours), since the architecture is identical except for the fusion operation (concat vs weighted average), making it a moderate-cost experiment relative to the budget.

Evidence: config_007 (pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is the best at 0.639 acc, clearly outperforming transformer aggregation (0.573) and concat fusion (0.619). Multimodal strongly beats RNA-only (0.639 vs 0.519). The main untested lever within the proven avgpool+weighted recipe is the image encoder: upgrading from ResNet50 to ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L could yield a meaningful accuracy gain since image features are a key multimodal signal. Question: Does a stronger image encoder (ViT-L) push accuracy above 0.639 while keeping the cheap, proven avgpool+weighted pipeline? This is a single-variable extension of the best config, making results interpretable. Cost: ViT-L is ~300M params vs ResNet50's ~25M, so I estimate ~18–25 GPU hours—moderately more expensive than config_007 (10.6) but far cheaper than the concat-fusion configs (~36). With 5 experiments remaining, this is the highest-value exploitation step: it tests the most impactful unexplored axis (image encoder quality) within the already-validated architecture, and a positive result would set up further refinement (e.g., RNA encoder upgrade) in subsequent runs.

The top-3 experiments (config_007: 0.639, config_026: 0.635, config_002: 0.619) all share avgpool aggregation + weighted/concat fusion + multiprofile, establishing that this architecture is the clear winner over transformer aggregation (0.573) and rna_only (0.519). The one major unexplored variable within this winning architecture is the RNA encoder: all top results use pca_n2000. Config_009 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is a clean single-variable swap from the best config (config_007), testing whether a learned variational RNA representation can outperform PCA while keeping the proven avgpool+weighted+resnet50 backbone. This is the highest-information experiment: if scvi_n200 improves accuracy, it opens a promising exploitation path for the remaining 4 experiments (e.g., pairing scvi with other image encoders); if it does not, PCA is confirmed as sufficient and we can focus remaining budget on fine-tuning other axes. Expected cost is similar to config_007 (~10–12 GPU hours) since the downstream architecture is identical and scvi_n200 produces the same 200-dim representation dimensionality.

The best result so far is config_009 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.6776, 5.90 GPU hrs). The key evidence is: (1) scvi_n200 substantially outperforms pca_n2000 (~4% gain), (2) avgpool beats transformer aggregation, and (3) weighted fusion beats concat. The main remaining uncertainty is whether imagenet_vit_l can match or exceed resnet50 as the image encoder in the scvi_n200 context. With pca_n2000, the two image encoders were nearly tied (0.6390 vs 0.6352), and imagenet_vit_l was cheaper (7.02 vs 10.60 GPU hrs). config_034 tests this exact swap while keeping all other settings at their proven-best values. If it matches or beats config_009, we get a cheaper top configuration; if it falls short, we confirm resnet50 is optimal and can direct the remaining 2 experiments toward other levers (e.g., singleprofile or scgpt). Expected relative cost: moderate, roughly 6–8 GPU hours (comparable to config_026's 7.02 hrs, since it uses imagenet_vit_l with avgpool+weighted fusion, avoiding the expensive concat pathway).

The current best (config_034, acc=0.706) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, and all evidence points to these being the optimal choices for each dimension. However, scgpt as an RNA encoder has never been tested in any multimodal setting. Config_012 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is the direct logical extension: it swaps only the RNA encoder to scgpt while keeping all other proven-best components. This tests whether scgpt's richer learned representations could surpass scvi_n200's 0.706 accuracy. If scgpt matches or exceeds scvi_n200, we gain a new best; if not, we confirm scvi_n200 is optimal and can use the final experiment for a minor refinement (e.g., config_032 to check transformer aggregation). This is the highest-information experiment remaining because it explores the last untested major design axis. Expected cost is moderate (~6-8 GPU hours), slightly higher than config_034 (4.82) due to scgpt's larger model size, but well within budget.

Evidence: config_034 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) is the clear best at 0.706 accuracy. Across all comparisons, avgpool has outperformed transformer (e.g., 0.639 vs 0.573 with pca_n2000+resnet50), but that gap was measured with PCA embeddings. scvi_n200 produces learned, richer representations that may benefit more from attention-based (transformer) aggregation to selectively weight profile interactions. Question: Can transformer aggregation with the strongest encoder pair (scvi_n200 + vit_l) close or surpass the avgpool result? Why this experiment: It is the single most informative untested variation of the best configuration—only the aggregation method changes. If it beats 0.706, it meaningfully improves the final answer; if it does not, it confirms avgpool is optimal and the remaining experiment can be spent on a longer-shot alternative (e.g., singleprofile). Expected relative cost: moderate, roughly 7–9 GPU hours (transformer adds attention computation over avgpool's 4.82 h, but vit_l and scvi_n200 are already in the pipeline), which is acceptable given the high information value.

The strongest evidence across 9 experiments points to scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer aggregation + multiprofile as the optimal architecture, with config_032 (weighted fusion) achieving 0.7250. The only untested variant of this proven-optimal combination is config_036, which swaps weighted fusion for concat. While weighted has generally outperformed concat (config_007 vs config_002), the interaction between transformer-generated contextual representations and concat fusion is untested and could yield a different inductive bias for the final classifier. As the final experiment, this is the highest-probability candidate to either beat 0.7250 or confirm config_032 as the best. Expected cost is similar to config_032 (~3.6 GPU hours) since the architecture is identical and only the fusion operation changes, bringing total budget to ~82.5 GPU hours.
